title: Built 1113 – 1150 CE
description: Raised as the state temple of Suryavarman II and dedicated to Vishnu. It was turned to Theravada Buddhist use in the fourteenth century and has never fallen out of worship since.

title: Built 11th – 12th century
description: Six radial routes ran out of Angkor. This one carried the court east to Preah Khan of Kompong Svay; the Preah Khan stele lists the rest houses and hospitals that stood along it.

title: Built late 12th – early 13th century
description: One of the largest and least restored of Jayavarman VII's foundations, with face towers and a gallery of multi-armed Lokesvara reliefs. On Cambodia's UNESCO tentative list.

title: Built 967 CE
description: Consecrated in 967 by the brahmin Yajnavaraha, tutor to Jayavarman V — the only major Angkorian temple not founded by a king, and the reason its carving is unlike anything else.

title: Built late 12th – early 13th century
description: The state temple of Jayavarman VII, set at the exact centre of his walled city of Angkor Thom. Founded as a Mahayana Buddhist temple, reworked for Hindu worship by his successor, and returned to Buddhist use later still.

title: Built 928 – 944 CE
description: Capital of the empire for sixteen years under Jayavarman IV, who raised the only stepped pyramid the Khmer ever built. Inscribed by UNESCO in 2023.
sourceReference: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Koh Ker (https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1667/)

title: Built 1917 – 1920
description: Opened under Sisowath in 1920, and holding the largest collection of Khmer sculpture anywhere — pre-Angkorian sixth century through to the post-Angkorian period, one room after another.

title: Built 7th century
description: A small Funan-era brick sanctuary dedicated to Shiva, built inside the cave and still standing.

title: Built 802 – c. 835 CE
description: Mahendraparvata, the mountain capital where Jayavarman II declared himself universal monarch in 802 — the act the Angkorian era is dated from. Lidar survey has since traced a full city plan under the forest.

title: Built 11th – 12th century
description: Jayavarman VII founded 102 arogayasala — hospital chapels — across the empire. The one at the east gate here is among the most complete anywhere, and the enclosure around it runs five kilometres a side.

title: Built 9th – 12th century
description: Four reigns of building spread along an 800-metre processional axis on the Dangrek escarpment, dedicated to Shiva. Inscribed by UNESCO in 2008.
sourceReference: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Preah Vihear (https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1224/)

title: Built 1866 – 1870
description: Built when Norodom I moved the capital from Oudong back to Chaktomuk, closing a chronology that had begun at Mahendraparvata a thousand years earlier. The Silver Pagoda beside it holds the royal regalia.

title: Built early 7th century
description: Ishanapura, capital of Chenla and the earliest Khmer city still standing above ground. Its octagonal brick towers are where Khmer temple architecture first found a form of its own.
sourceReference: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Sambor Prei Kuk (https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1532/)

title: Built late 12th century
description: One of more than a hundred bridges thrown across the royal roads under Jayavarman VII. Twenty-one corbelled arches carry it 87 metres over the Chikreng river.

title: Built 1186 CE
description: Founded as Rajavihara, a Buddhist monastery and university dedicated to the king's mother. Its foundation stele records that 12,640 people served the temple directly.
